hans.contract_flavor: A woodcutter named Hans, found at the wood-line. Villagers cry wolf. The old folk hide their faces.

mill.contract_flavor: The miller of Furt was found beside his wheel, broken like kindling. His prentice ran half-mad to the bailiff and would say only "it stood up — God, it stood up."

case_003.contract_flavor: Ernst Hübner, master tailor, found slumped against his fitting mirror. Expression serene. Three rings missing from his fingers. He measured twice and cut once — in cloth and in life.

case_004.contract_flavor: Willem Roth found forty feet from the treeline. Deep claw lacerations. Expression of pure terror. The snow remembers everything — and whatever did this was not in a hurry.

case_005.contract_flavor: Petra Holz, bookkeeper, found between two barrels in a locked cellar. No external wounds. Body contorted. She had the only key. Whatever was in there with her had been waiting long before she came down.

case_006.contract_flavor: Lord Aldric Fenn found dead at his desk. No wounds, no struggle. Glass of wine half-drunk. Body cold far beyond what the time of death allows — the room is warm but he is ice-cold to the touch.

case_007.contract_flavor: Jakob Weiss, moneylender, found at his counting table. The vault is empty — no forced entry. Two clean cuts at the throat, surgical not ragged. Whatever killed him, he let through the door himself.

case_008.contract_flavor: Rolf Huber, east-gate watchman, found dead at the drainage channel. Twin puncture wounds at the throat, skin faintly green-tinged. He checked that culvert every night at the same hour. Something learned his schedule.

case_009.contract_flavor: Three charcoal burners found dead at their winter pit, deep in the Black Forest. No blade wounds — crushed. The third body was moved after death. Whatever came out of the deep forest was not in a hurry. The charcoal pit still burns.

case_010.contract_flavor: Heinrich Braun, cloth merchant, found dead in his chamber. No wounds. Expression serene. His gold family chain is gone. His wife says a beautiful woman visited twice this week — pale, dark hair. Heinrich would not say her name.
